were prepared by arc-melting a mixture of pure metals (purity, >99.9 weight %), TiN (99.9 weight %), and TiO2 (99.9 weight %) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere. The ingots were re-melted at least eight times to ensure chemical homogeneity.
Melted alloys were eventually drop-cast into a water-cooled copper mold with a dimension of 10 mm by 10 mm by 60 mm.

Because of the high configuration entropy and severely distorted lattices of HEAs (50), atomic position switches of interstitials in these matrices are impeded by the high atomic-scale distortion fields (51).
These interstitial atoms in the severely distorted matrices with complex chemical short-range orders result in high strengthening, large ductility, and good high-temperature damping properties.

mechanisms.name: ordered interstitial complexes mediated strain hardening

evidence.quote: Via Snoek relaxation and ordered interstitial complexes mediated strain hardening, the damping capacity of these HEAs is as high as 0.030
This mechanism leads to strongly broadened Snoek-type peaks.
